chunks: And from him from Muhammad ibn 'Isa who said:

Abu 'Amr wrote to him saying: Inform me, O my master, that perhaps the crescent of the month of Ramadan is obscure to us, so we do not see it, and we see the sky has no impediment, so the people fast and we fast with them. And a group of astronomers/calculators near us say that it is seen on that very night in Egypt, Ifriqiya, and Al-Andalus. Is it permissible, O my master, what the astronomers said in this matter, so that the obligation differs among the people of the regions, so their fasting is contrary to our fasting and their breaking of the fast is contrary to our breaking of the fast?
So the Imam (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Do not fast on the basis of doubt; break the fast upon its sighting, and fast upon its sighting.'

key_terms.هِلاَلُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Crescent of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on fasting when the crescent is not visible locally but is visible in other countries?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the jurisprudential dilemma of 'Ikhtilaf al-Masalik' (divergence of sighting paths) when the crescent is visible in one region but obscured in another. The Imam’s directive to 'do not fast on doubt' emphasizes that local visibility is the primary criterion for the individual, thereby validating independent fasting practices across different geographical areas rather than enforcing a single global date.
